1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with comfortable letter and line spacing and no visual crowding.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case, no italics or all-caps, and appear only as short separate sentences or labels.

3.why: Content is presented in a single centered card with large tap targets and ample whitespace that fits a mobile viewport.

4.why: Every instruction is one or two plain-language sentences (e.g., “Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone.”).

5.why: Academic test codes and a recovery-code placeholder (ABCD-EFGH-IJKL-MNPQ) illustrate expected format, though not every field has an inline example.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than a brief paragraph before the primary action is available.

7.why: The long setup secret and each recovery code are rendered as selectable plain text in boxes, allowing copy-and-paste.

8.why: No QR code is ever displayed; the UI explicitly states a QR code is not required and only manual secret entry is offered.

9.why: Standard labelled text inputs are used throughout, which browsers and password managers can autofill; no custom widgets block them.

10.why: Page headings name the current step and the blue primary button is visually dominant, though no step-number indicator is present.

11.why: Each screen presents exactly one main task and one primary call-to-action button.

12.why: Success feedback is explicit (“MFA is active”, “Recovery code accepted. It cannot be used again.”) and states what is possible next.

13.why: “Start again”, “Cancel setup”, and “Generate new recovery codes” let the user retry or re-request without lock-out or penalty.

14.why: The observed error (“We could not complete that request. Please try again.”) avoids blame but does not name the concrete problem or a specific fix.

15.why: No reading time-limit exists; the SMS code allows five minutes and TOTP follows the normal 30-second window, which is generous enough for entry.
